rationale: While cerebellar ataxia and lower limb spasticity are consistently documented across all reported cohorts of NKX6-2-related disorder (SPAX8), the hypothesis that epilepsy and nystagmus selectively cluster with diffuse central hypomyelination is directly contradicted by multicenter observational data. Chelban et al. (2020) demonstrated that epilepsy can occur in patients lacking overt hypomyelination, while individuals with diffuse hypomyelination may present without seizures. Furthermore, nystagmus and developmental delay appear across multiple phenotypic strata, including milder childhood-onset presentations.

evidence.text: All seven patients identified across three original families presented with early-onset spastic ataxia, but hypomyelination was present in only one family while the others showed cerebellar atrophy alone.

source.title: Mutations in NKX6-2 cause progressive spastic ataxia and hypomyelination
source.journal: The American Journal of Human Genetics
source.quote: We report seven individuals with an early-onset spastic-ataxia phenotype. The individuals come from three families of different ethnic backgrounds. Affected members of two families had childhood onset disease with very slow progression. They are still alive in their 30s and 40s and show predominant ataxia and cerebellar atrophy features on imaging. Affected members of the third family had a similar but earlier-onset presentation associated with brain hypomyelination.

evidence.text: Detailed clinical characterization of an expanded cohort demonstrated that epilepsy can occur in individuals without overt hypomyelination, and diffuse hypomyelination can occur in the absence of seizures, disproving strict selective clustering.

source.title: Genetic and phenotypic characterization of NKX6‐2‐related spastic ataxia and hypomyelination
source.quote: The phenotypic and neuroimaging expression in NKX6-2 is described and it is shown that phenotypes with epilepsy in the absence of overt hypomyelination and diffuse hypomyelination without seizures can occur.

evidence.text: Nystagmus is documented not only in severe neonatal presentations but also as an integral component of cerebellar findings in milder childhood-onset presentations.

source.title: NKX6-2-Related Disorder
source.quote: At the milder end of the spectrum is normal achievement of early motor milestones in the first year of life followed by slowly progressive complex spastic ataxia with pyramidal findings (spasticity with increased muscle tone and difficulty with gait and fine motor coordination) and cerebellar findings (nystagmus, extraocular movement disorder, dysarthria, titubation, and ataxia) with loss of developmental milestones.

evidence.text: Siblings with a novel missense variant presented with global developmental delay, nystagmus, and spasticity alongside axonal peripheral neuropathy and cerebellar white matter involvement.

source.title: Expanding the clinical and neuroimaging features of NKX6-2-related hereditary spastic ataxia type 8
source.quote: identified a novel missense variant, c.501C > G; p.(Phe167Leu), in two affected siblings with main manifestations of global developmental delay, motor regression, hypotonia, clonus in lower limbs and muscle bulk atrophy especially in the upper limbs, spasticity and contracture, scoliosis, hip dislocation, oculomotor apraxia, horizontal and vertical nystagmus.

conflicts: Chelban et al. (2020) specifically reported that epilepsy occurs in the absence of overt hypomyelination, while patients with diffuse hypomyelination can present without seizures, which contradicts the hypothesis that epilepsy selectively clusters with diffuse hypomyelination.
Nystagmus is documented across both mild (childhood-onset) and severe (neonatal-onset) ends of the disease spectrum rather than being restricted to cases with hypomyelination.

new_directions.question_text: What specific MRI neuroimaging markers (e.g., T2 hypointensity patterns, cerebellar volume ratio) reliably differentiate NKX6-2-related spastic ataxia from Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease and other hypomyelinating leukodystrophies?
new_directions.rationale: Clinical features overlap broadly across early-onset leukodystrophies; establishing discriminating radiologic signatures would allow clinicians to distinguish SPAX8 earlier in the diagnostic workup.

new_directions.question_text: Does variant class (truncating/nonsense vs. homeobox domain missense) correlate quantitatively with the degree of myelination impairment on neuroimaging?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying the genotype-phenotype relationship will explain why some patients manifest with isolated cerebellar atrophy while others develop severe diffuse hypomyelination.
